rounds.plan: Rotate in place to survey all six hex directions for the beacon and open paths.
Advance along the apparent central open lane and inspect the new view.
Turn away from the mirrored dead end and retrace through the known opening.
The retrace cell has a mirror ahead; turn toward the side passage and inspect it.
The front is a mirror; survey the other headings from this junction before moving.
Turn toward the only view with a distant reflection, indicating an open passage, and advance.
Probe successive headings to find an open passage beyond the mirrors.
Probe the two untested side passages from this cell, avoiding the known mirrored walls.
A close reflection marks a mirror ahead; survey the other five headings for a real opening.
Return to the only heading with a distant corridor view and advance into it.
The forward cell is mirrored; probe the next counterclockwise passage.
Test the next side opening around this mirrored cell, then continue to the following junction.
Both tested headings are mirrored; probe the next untested side passage.
The forward passage is reflected; turn to the next untested exit and advance.
Continue around the mirrored cell to find an open passage.
Continue wall-following around the mirrored dead end to reach unexplored passages.
The close reflection marks a wall ahead; turn left and probe the next passage.
Continue left-hand wall-following to escape the mirrored dead ends and reach new passages.
Continue deterministic left-hand wall-following through the mirrored corridors to reach the actual beacon.
Break the two-cell backtracking loop by probing the untested clockwise passage.
Probe the remaining untested clockwise heading to escape the two-cell loop.
Switch to right-hand wall-following to leave the repeated corridor and search for the actual beacon.
Reverse out of the dead end, then keep straight through the next cell instead of immediately backtracking.
The repeated moves were a two-cell loop. From the new cell, probe its two untested counterclockwise exits.
Only the reverse heading remains unprobed at this cell; take it to reach a new junction.
Probe the final untested side exit; if blocked, only the known return passage remains.
Return through the known corridor, then probe the untested forward exit at the far cell instead of looping back.
The corridor now ends at a mirror; probe the left-hand exit from this newly reached cell.
Probe the unexplored clockwise exits from this cell, avoiding the known return passage.
The mirror ahead is blocked; probe the four unexplored side headings while preserving the known return route.
Leave this dead end, then take the previously untested straight branch beyond the earlier two-cell loop.
Probe the one remaining untested exit from this cell to leave the repeated corridor.
Retrace to the previous cell and probe its remaining untested side passage.
Survey all remaining headings from this mirrored dead end to identify its actual open exits.
Advance toward the distant open corridor view rather than the close mirror reflection.
Probe the left-hand exit; after moving, continue straight when possible instead of automatically turning back.
The front is a confirmed mirror; probe the next counterclockwise heading while avoiding the known return passage.
Correct the search order: return to the arrival heading and test straight before considering backtracking.
Test the untested clockwise exit from this mirrored cell.
Use a varied long random walk to break mirrored loops and search new cells for the actual beacon.
Turn left to inspect the next side of the mirrored cell for a genuine opening.
The front is a close mirror wall; rotate to inspect the next side for an open passage.
The front-facing self-image confirms a mirror ahead; turn left to find a direction without an immediate reflection.
A close front-facing reflection indicates a mirror ahead; turn left and probe that passage.
The reflected frontal self-image is a wall; probe the next clockwise direction for an actual opening.
The immediate frontal reflection is a mirror wall; survey the other headings for a genuine corridor and beacon.
Turn to the side corridor with no close self-reflection and advance; the opposite passage is the known return route.
The close frontal reflection marks a mirror ahead; turn left to find an unreflected opening.
The close frontal self-image confirms a mirror ahead; survey all other headings for a real opening or beacon.
The centered reflection is several cells away, indicating an open corridor ahead; continue straight.
The close frontal self-image confirms a mirror wall; survey the other headings for a genuine opening or beacon.
Take the newly found open side passage, away from the known return corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirror ahead; survey the other headings for a genuine passage or beacon.
Turn toward the only view with a distant reflection, indicating an open passage, and advance.
The close frontal self-image confirms a mirror ahead; survey the other headings for a genuine passage or beacon.
Avoid the close mirrors and take the non-return corridor with the distant reflection.
The close frontal self-reflection is a mirror wall; survey the other headings for the continuing corridor.
Only the opposite corridor is open; the other five views show close mirrored self-images. Continue through it.
The close frontal self-image marks a mirror ahead; survey the other headings for a real opening or green beacon.
Two headings show open corridors; take the left-hand branch instead of reversing into the repeated passage.
The immediate frontal reflection is a mirror wall; survey the other headings for the real passage or beacon.
Take the corridor with the distant reflection; the other headings show close mirror walls.
Return through the known opening, then make a full five-view survey from the previous cell to identify its other exits.
Advance along the corridor showing a distant rather than close self-reflection.
The close frontal self-image marks a mirror; survey the other headings for an open passage or green beacon.
Turn toward the open corridor with the distant reflection and advance.
The close frontal self-image confirms a mirror ahead; survey the other headings for a genuine passage or green beacon.
Take the open corridor with the distant reflection; avoid the close mirrored self-images.
The frontal self-image is a nearby mirror; survey the other headings for an open corridor or the actual green beacon.
Take the only open corridor, identified by the distant reflection in the third survey view.
The close frontal self-image marks a mirror wall; survey the other headings for a real passage or green beacon.
Take the other open branch instead of the known return corridor; close frontal reflections are mirrored walls.
The close frontal self-image marks a mirror wall; survey the other headings for an open passage or green beacon.
Take the corridor with the distant reflection, then survey the new cell for the beacon and exits.
Use left-first exhaustive wall-following, trying each hex heading until one move succeeds, to escape loops and reach the beacon.
Survey all six headings from this cell to identify a genuine corridor and any beacon without risking another collision.
Turn toward the heading with the distant centered reflection, then advance one cell into that apparent corridor.
The close centered reflection marks a wall, so reverse and return through the known open cell before choosing another exit.
The backtracking move faces a wall. Rotate right to check the adjacent heading for the other genuine exit.
The current heading is a mirrored wall; rotate right to inspect the next possible exit from this cell.
The close frontal reflection marks a wall, so rotate right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall; rotate right to inspect the next heading.
Five headings have been blocked; turn right once more to inspect the final untested exit from this cell.
This is the dead-end cell with only its entrance open. Turn back to that entrance, return one cell, then inspect a new heading there.
The centered reflection is now small and one cell ahead, indicating the open entrance. Advance through it and reassess the next cell.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect an adjacent exit from this cell.
The distant centered self-reflection and receding floor lines indicate an open corridor ahead. Advance one cell.
The centered reflection remains distant and the corridor ahead appears open. Continue forward one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for an open corridor.
The receding corridor and distant centered reflection indicate an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The distant centered reflection and receding corridor indicate the path ahead is open. Continue forward one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for an open corridor.
The close centered self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Rotate left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks another mirrored wall. Rotate left to inspect the next heading for the open exit.
The receding corridor and small centered self-reflection indicate an open heading. Advance one cell.
The centered self-reflection is distant and the corridor recedes ahead, indicating an open path. Continue forward one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the adjacent heading for an open corridor.
The centered self-reflection is distant and the corridor clearly recedes ahead, so advance one cell.
The centered reflection is distant and the corridor ahead appears open. Advance one cell while watching for the green beacon.
The close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The large frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The small centered reflection and receding corridor indicate an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The small centered reflection and receding corridor indicate an open path ahead. Continue forward one cell.

The distant centered self-reflection and receding corridor indicate an open path ahead. Advance one cell.

The small centered self-reflection and receding central corridor indicate an open path ahead. Continue forward one cell.
The large frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect a new heading for an open corridor.
The central corridor recedes clearly with a distant self-reflection, indicating an open path. Advance one cell.
The small centered reflection and receding central corridor indicate an open path ahead. Continue forward one cell.
The large close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect an adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The central corridor recedes with a distant centered reflection, indicating an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the adjacent heading for the open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks another mirrored wall. Turn right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The centered self-reflection is distant and the corridor recedes ahead, indicating an open path. Advance one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the next heading for a genuine corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Rotate right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The central corridor is open with a distant self-reflection. Advance one cell and reassess for the green beacon.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The central corridor recedes with a distant self-reflection, indicating an open path. Advance one cell.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The small centered self-reflection and receding central corridor indicate an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for an open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The distant centered self-reflection and receding central corridor indicate an open path. Advance one cell and reassess.
The centered reflection remains distant and the central corridor is open. Advance one cell toward the next junction.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the next heading for a genuine opening.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The distant centered self-reflection and receding central corridor indicate an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The central corridor remains open with a distant self-reflection. Advance one cell and reassess for the actual green beacon.
The centered self-reflection is distant and the central corridor remains open. Advance one cell while watching for the actual green beacon.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall ahead. Turn left to inspect the next heading for a genuine opening.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The central corridor recedes with a distant self-reflection, indicating an open path. Advance one cell.
The distant centered reflection and receding corridor indicate an open path ahead. Advance one cell and reassess for the green beacon.
The large frontal self-reflection indicates a mirrored wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the adjacent heading for an open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn right to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The central corridor recedes with a distant self-reflection, indicating an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The distant centered reflection and receding corridor indicate an open cell ahead. Advance once, then vary the next junction choice to escape the repeating route.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect a new heading for an open corridor.
The large close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The central corridor is open with a distant self-reflection. Advance one cell and reassess for the actual green beacon.
Leave the repeating junction loop, return to the far corridor, and probe its unexplored side passage toward the beacon.
The current heading is a confirmed wall. Turn right toward the receding corridor seen during the survey and advance one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine corridor.
The central corridor recedes with a distant self-reflection, indicating an open path ahead. Advance one cell.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the adjacent heading for a genuine opening.
This heading is another close mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next side for an unexplored open passage.
The close frontal self-reflection marks a mirrored wall. Turn left to inspect the next heading for an open corridor.
The centered reflection is one cell ahead with visible floor space between, indicating an open passage. Advance one cell.
Resume the deterministic left-hand wall traversal for a longer sweep so it can pass beyond the repeated local loop and cover the remaining passages.
The current heading is confirmed blocked by a close mirror wall. Rotate right to inspect the adjacent passage without repeating the collision.
The close centered self-reflection indicates another mirrored wall ahead. Rotate right again to look for an open heading.
The centered robot image is smaller and separated by a clear floor cell, indicating an open passage ahead. Advance one cell.
A large close frontal self-reflection fills the passage ahead, indicating a nearby mirror wall. Turn left to inspect another heading.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Turn left to inspect the next adjacent passage.
The close frontal self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Turn left to inspect the next passage.
The close centered self-reflection shows a mirror wall directly ahead. Continue rotating left to find an open passage.
The close centered reflection indicates a blocked heading. Rotate back toward the known open reverse passage and move through it to leave this mirrored pocket.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall ahead. Turn right to inspect an adjacent passage.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Turn right to inspect the next adjacent passage.
The close centered self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Rotate right to inspect another passage.
Probe the current passage with one forward step; the centered reflection has visible floor space ahead and no green beacon is visible.
The close centered self-reflection indicates a wall ahead. Begin a right-hand wall-following probe by turning right and testing that passage.
The current heading is confirmed blocked. Rotate left to inspect the adjacent passage without repeating the collision.
The frontal mirror is close and the right-hand passage is blocked. Turn left and probe the remaining adjacent corridor.
The current heading is confirmed blocked. Turn left to inspect the next untested adjacent passage.
Two adjacent headings are confirmed blocked. Rotate to the remaining untested side passage and probe it before retreating.
The current heading is confirmed blocked. Return to the previous heading, where the smaller reflection and clear floor indicate an open passage, and advance one cell.
The close centered self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Turn left to inspect the adjacent passage.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Turn left to inspect the next adjacent passage.
The small centered self-reflection has clear floor space ahead, indicating an open corridor. Advance one cell.
The centered self-reflection is small and distant with clear floor space ahead, indicating an open corridor. Advance one cell.
The centered reflection remains distant with clear floor space ahead, indicating an open corridor. Continue forward one cell.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall ahead. Turn right to inspect the adjacent passage.
The large close self-reflection shows a mirror wall directly ahead. Rotate right to inspect the next passage.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Rotate right toward the reverse corridor to find an open passage.
The reverse corridor is open and the other inspected headings are mirrored walls. Retrace three known-clear cells to reach the earlier junction, then choose a different branch.
The three-step retrace reached a close mirror wall. Turn right to inspect an untested side passage.
The large close self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Rotate right to inspect the next adjacent passage.
The close centered self-reflection indicates a mirror wall directly ahead. Rotate right to inspect another passage.
The centered reflection is distant with clear floor space ahead, indicating an open corridor. Advance one cell.
The centered reflection is distant with clear floor space ahead, indicating an open corridor. Continue forward through the passage.
The forward wall is confirmed. Turn right and probe the adjacent passage for an exit toward the beacon.
Both the original and right-hand headings are confirmed walls. Rotate two steps left to probe the opposite adjacent passage.
The close centered self-reflection indicates a mirror wall ahead. Rotate right and probe the adjacent passage for an open route.
The current heading is confirmed blocked. Use the final planning turn for an extended alternating wall-following sweep to search remaining passages for the actual beacon.
A close mirror blocks the apparent forward view. Probe the right-hand passage, then continue through any open corridor in search of the actual beacon.
